description: Bluetooth game and system audio for A2DP SBC headsets using the console Bluetooth. Control WebUI on port 8090.

changelog: Fixed Bluetooth headphones failing to connect cleanly on consoles with a MediaTek chip (#34).
What is new
The HearBridge tile is now in the Media tab. The old tile in the Games tab is removed automatically the first time this version loads.
The tile now opens even when there is no internet, and it shows a short message if HearBridge is not loaded yet.
HearBridge keeps running even after the internet disconnects, or with no internet at all.
The tile and the page are now simply called HearBridge.
Added name hints so Huawei FreeClip and FreeBuds are recognised in the scan list.
A saved headset should now connect faster after you turn it on or take it out of its case, as long as the HearBridge page is open in a browser.
The diagnostics page (/api/diag) now shows the last log lines with times, and the log from the previous run. This makes bug reports much easier to read.
Not fixed in this version

Controller problems (a controller that does not reconnect, or stays unresponsive after switching users or using headphones). Controllers share the same Bluetooth chip as the console, so they are hard to solve. For now, play with a fully charged controller and turn off controller auto power off in the console settings.
Download: HearBridge-PS5-1.3.0.elf (one file for every PS5, Marvell/NXP and MediaTek)
Send it to your loader on port 9021 like before.
What's new in 1.3.0
Game profiles (new)
HearBridge detects the running game by itself and shows its name and cover art.
Each game can have its own sound: EQ, preset, boost, volume and night mode.
The game's profile loads by itself when the game starts, and your usual sound comes back when it closes.
Each headset keeps its own profile for the same game. For example, the same game can have heavy bass on one headset and a balanced sound on another, and each one loads its own when it connects.
Save up to 32 games, with up to 4 headsets per game.
If the connected headset has no profile for the game yet, the game's latest profile from another headset is used, without overwriting it.

What's new: home-screen icon and "already running" fixes

The home-screen icon is reinstalled on every run. If you deleted the HearBridge icon, running HearBridge again brings it back. Before, it stayed missing because HearBridge thought it was already installed.
Re-registering an icon that is already there is treated as success, so you don't get a false "icon could not be added" message.
No false "already running" after a crash, a forced quit or a leftover lock file. The lock is released automatically when HearBridge exits for any reason, so a new run always starts.
If HearBridge really is already running, running it again still refreshes the icon before showing "already running".
If /data/hearbridge is not writable, you now get a separate message instead of "already running".

Firmware 13.60 (experimental): HearBridge-PS5-1.0.1-fw13.60.elf
If you are on firmware 13.60 and get no HearBridge icon on the home screen, try this file instead of HearBridge-PS5-1.0.1.elf. Same version (1.0.1), same page and audio. It:
is meant to fix the missing home-screen icon on newer firmware (the icon is registered with a fallback install call and system rights, and registered again if it went missing);

adds diagnostics: /data/hearbridge/diag.txt and http://:8090/api/diag (firmware, console model, each install step with its result code, USB/Bluetooth devices, audio libraries), plus an on-screen message if the icon could not be added;
keeps the page and diagnostics up when Bluetooth cannot start, and no longer says "already running" when /data/hearbridge is not writable.
Not tested on a real console yet. As far as I can tell it should also work on other firmwares, but that is unverified. If it does not work, please report it with the log files.

Tested on: HearBridge was developed and tested on a PS5 fat (original model, CFI-10xx) running firmware 10.20. Other models (Slim, Pro, later fat revisions) and other firmwares are untested and may use a different Bluetooth chip, so reports from them are welcome.

Download: HearBridge-PS5-1.0.0.elf
Streams game and system audio to A2DP headphones or speakers over the PS5's built-in Bluetooth (SBC).
Web page on port 8090 (11 languages): scan (about 20 s), connect, disconnect, forget, boost and headset volume (AVRCP).
Manual connections only: nothing connects in the background.
Run: send the ELF to elfldr on port 9021, then open http://:8090.
